description.value: A 42-hectare nature reserve on Galiano Island protecting one of the last intact tracts of mature and old-growth Coastal Douglas-fir forest in the Southern Gulf Islands. The reserve stretches from Trincomali Channel to the island's central ridgeline, encompassing rare Garry Oak woodlands, creek and wetland habitats, and 600 metres of undeveloped coastline. Established in 2024 by the Galiano Conservancy Association through Canada's Old Growth Nature Fund.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website confirms this is a 42-hectare nature reserve on Galiano Island established in 2024, featuring old-growth Coastal Douglas-fir forest, trails, and 600m of undeveloped coastline. No visitor amenities (bike parking, water, washrooms) are mentioned anywhere on the website or in OSM tags. The OSM community field says 'Chemainus' but the coordinates (48.92, -123.45) and all website content place this on Galiano Island — a clear data error. The OSM operator field has a typo ('Assosiation' instead of 'Association').

enrichment_extras.notes: The Galiano Conservancy also operates the nearby Millard Learning Centre and a Mid-Island Protected Areas Network with trail access. A cyclist visiting Galiano could combine multiple GCA properties. The reserve itself appears to be undeveloped conservation land with trail access but no services.
